sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by anti-FLAG staining under non-permeabilized conditions (L4); receptor activation assays and radioligand binding showed wild-type-like properties for the FLAG-tagged construct (L2).
sites.rationale: NPY4R has no endogenous signal peptide (topology residues 1–40 are extracellular, raw topology begins with 'O'); therefore exactly one extracellular N-terminus exists and the FLAG tag prepends before residue 1 (M), giving insert_after_residue=0 by topology derivation. The N-terminal extracellular span is 40 residues long, placing the tag well above the 3-residue minimum from TM1 (which begins at residue 41). Python confirmed residue 1 = M and residue 40 = V (last extracellular residue before TM1). Functional validation from L2 (same paper, same tag architecture) and surface confirmation from L4 together support surface_and_function. Full-length human Y4R with an N-terminal FLAG epitope tag was cloned into pcDNA3.1 for mammalian cell expression and functional assays (L3); cell surface expression was confirmed by anti-FLAG antibody staining of non-permeabilized cells (L4); a parallel construct (L2) with the same N-terminal FLAG tag (preceded by an exogenous HA signal peptide for insect-cell expression) was validated by receptor activation assays and radioligand binding showing wild-type-like properties.

sources.claim: The N-terminal flag-tagged wild-type receptor, receptor mutants, and a chimeric G protein Gα Δ6qi4myr , which redirects the Gα i signaling pathway to the Gα q phospholipase C pathway ( 60 ), were cloned into the expression vector pcDNA3.1/V5-His-TOPO (Invitrogen).

literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) are from the same publication (PMC9067930) and all support the same N-terminal FLAG tag site on NPY4R. L1 and L2 describe insect-cell cryo-EM constructs with an exogenous HA signal peptide followed by FLAG; L3 and L4 describe the wild-type mammalian pcDNA3.1 construct with N-terminal FLAG. No ledger line supports any insertion in ECL1 (101–115), ECL2 (177–212), or ECL3 (287–301). The C-terminal twin-strep-tag (L1, L2) replaces residues S343–I375, which fall entirely within the intracellular C-terminal tail (topology: 326–375 intracellular); it is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports any insertion that abrogates function.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal residues S343–I375 were replaced with a twin-strep-tag for cryo-EM purification; the entire C-terminal tail (residues 326–375) is intracellular per topology, so this tag is not on the extracellular face.
